candidates.name: Rasmussen's encephalitis
support_spans: recurrent seizures, left-sided weakness, and developmental delays
marked asymmetry of the cerebral hemispheres, with significant atrophy of the right cerebral hemisphere
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms and brain imaging results are consistent with Rasmussen's encephalitis, a rare inflammatory neurological disease.

candidates.name: Sturge-Weber syndrome
support_spans: left-sided weakness
ipsilateral calvarial thickening
candidates.why: The patient's left-sided weakness and calvarial thickening are consistent with Sturge-Weber syndrome, a disorder characterized by abnormal blood vessels in the brain.

candidates.name: Cerebral vasculitis
support_spans: marked asymmetry of the cerebral hemispheres, with significant atrophy of the right cerebral hemisphere
candidates.why: The patient's brain imaging results suggest cerebral vasculitis, a condition characterized by inflammation of the blood vessels in the brain.

candidates.name: Hemimegalencephaly
support_spans: marked asymmetry of the cerebral hemispheres
candidates.why: The patient's brain imaging results are consistent with hemimegalencephaly, a condition characterized by abnormal growth of one half of the brain.

candidates.name: Tuberous sclerosis complex
support_spans: brain magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated marked asymmetry of the cerebral hemispheres
candidates.why: A definitive diagnosis of tuberous sclerosis complex would require imaging findings such as cortical tubers, subependymal nodules, or subependymal giant cell astrocytomas.

candidates.name: Porencephaly
support_spans: cystic encephalomalacia surrounded by gliosis
candidates.why: The patient's brain imaging results are consistent with porencephaly, a condition characterized by cystic cavities in the brain.
